data.command: What is T1567 Web Service Exfiltration technique?

data.text:
# T1567 — Exfiltration Over Web Service

**T1567** is a technique in the MITRE ATT&CK framework under the **Exfiltration** tactic (TA0010). It describes adversaries stealing data by sending it to **legitimate, third-party web services** rather than to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

## Core Concept

Instead of exfiltrating data to a suspicious C2 server (which defenders can block or flag), attackers abuse trusted services that are already common in enterprise traffic — cloud storage, code repositories, paste sites, chat platforms. This makes exfiltration traffic blend in with normal business activity.

## Sub-techniques

| ID | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T1567.000 | Exfiltration to Code Repository | Data pushed to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, etc. via commits, gists, or issues |
| T1567.001 | Exfiltration to Cloud Storage | Uploads to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, MEGA, S3 buckets |
| T1567.002 | Exfiltration to Text Storage Sites | Data posted to pastebin-style sites (Pastebin, Ghostbin, hastebin) |
| T1567.003 | Exfiltration to Webhook | Data sent to Discord/Slack webhooks, Telegram bots, or similar |
| T1567.004 | Exfiltration over WebSocket | Data streamed over persistent WebSocket connections to external services |

## Why Attackers Use It

- **Trusted domains** — traffic to `api.github.com` or `discord.com` rarely triggers domain-based blocking
- **Encryption by default** — TLS to legitimate services hides content from basic inspection
- **No infrastructure cost** — no need to register domains or stand up servers that could be attributed/seized
- **Blends with legitimate use** — many orgs genuinely use these tools daily

## Real-World Examples

- Malware families using **Telegram Bot API** or **Discord webhooks** as exfil channels (very common in commodity stealers)
- APT actors staging stolen files in **Dropbox/Google Drive** accounts
- Ransomware groups leaking data via **MEGA** or paste sites
- Tools using **GitHub gists** to smuggle out reconnaissance data

## Detection Ideas

- Alert on **unusual processes** (e.g., `rundll32.exe`, Office apps, scripts) making connections to cloud storage/paste APIs
- Monitor **data volume anomalies** — large uploads to web services from endpoints that don't normally do so
- Use **DLP** and TLS inspection where feasible to inspect content bound for external services
- Baseline which SaaS tenants are sanctioned; flag uploads to **non-corporate accounts**
- Watch for API patterns like `api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendDocument` or Discord webhook URLs in process telemetry

## Mitigations

- **M1021 — Restrict Web-Based Content**: block or restrict access to unsanctioned cloud storage, paste sites, and webmail
- Enforce **CASB / proxy policies** allowing only corporate tenants
- Egress filtering and DLP at the network boundary

Want me to go deeper on any sub-technique, detection engineering (e.g., Sigma/Splunk queries), or how specific malware implements this?
